items.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010
items.q: It’s interesting, Eric Alexander said — I think he placed second in the Thelonious Monk competition also

ctx.x: Yeah people ask me all the time. And you know it’s hard because I had a lucky break. I mean I was playing gigs in Manhattan and doing all of that for several years before the Monk competition, but then I did it and I had a break. It’s really hard to get noticed. It’s really hard. Because it’s not like head honchos of record companies are going and sitting in the little jazz club with their cigar just waiting to discover the next big thing. That doesn’t happen. So it’s hard. So I always tell people to watch for…

It’s interesting, Eric Alexander said — I think he placed second in the Thelonious Monk competition also, behind Joshua Redman. And he said six months later he was working in a cubicle selling medical supplies or something. Like he didn’t have that — whatever happened for you did not necessarily happen for him. Maybe it’s different for vocalists.

It’s different when you are a super young vocalist. And what happened that year sort of got a lot of press too, because they changed the age limit and so the winner of the competition, Terry Thornton, was over 40 years older than I was. She was first and I was second. She was over sixty and I was twenty. So that big gap got a lot of attention. And plus I got up there and I was really confident and I had, you know, charts for the guys and was an experienced musician and had no problem doing what I was doing and…
